And quickly she let downe the tankard vpon her arme, and gaue him drinke. † And when he had druncke, she added : but for thy camels alſo I wil drawe water, til al doe drinke. † And powring our the tankard into the troughes, she ranne backe to the wel to drawe water : and being drawen gaue it to al the camels. † But he muſing beheld her with ſilence, deſirous to know whether our Lord had made his iourney proſperous, or not. † And after that the camels had drunck, the man plucked forth golden carelettes, weying two ſicles: and as manie braceletts of tenne ſicles weight. † And he ſaid to her: whoſe daughter art thou? shew me : is there anie place in thy fathers houſe to lodge? † who anſwered: I am the daughter of Bathuel, the ſonne of Melcha, whom she bare ro Nachor. † And she added, ſaying: Of ſtrawe alſo and hay we haue good ſtore, and a large place to lodge in. † The man bowed him ſelfe, and adored our Lord, † ſaying : Bleſſed be the Lord God of my lord Abraham, rhat hath not taken away his mercie & truth from my lord, and hath brought me the ſtreight way into the houſe hauing pet- haps manie of my lords brother. † The maide therfore ranne, and re- wues and e- ported into ‖ her mothers houſe al things thatſhe had heard. uerie one a And Rebecca had a brother named Laban, who in al haiſt ſeueral houſs went forth to the man, where the fountaine was. † And ſhe went to her mother when he had ſeene the eareletts and braceletts in his ſiſters houſe.
